title: upgrade attention kernels to FlashAttnV2 + fused QKV ops and rotary/rope optimizations
author: Ethan Park
release_notes: Performance: Upgraded attention kernels to FlashAttentionV2 with fused QKV/rope ops and improved KV-batching integration. Expect 20-45% throughput improvements and 10-30% lower p99 latency for long-context workloads. No API changes. Rollout: staged canary with automatic fallback to previous kernels.
description: Context: Long-running work to reduce per-token cost and tail latency for long-context serving. This PR replaces the older attention implementation with an integrated FlashAttentionV2 path and applies several fused-op and rotary/ROPE optimizations. Motivation: reduce memory copies, fuse Q/K/V projection + rotary position application, and expose a scheduling hint so the runtime dispatcher can better prioritize KV-heavy streams. Summary of changes: 1) Add FlashAttnV2 kernels (cuda/aten) and build flags; 2) Implement fused QKV + rotary application to avoid extra memory passes; 3) Integrate kernel selection into the scheduler so requests marked as `kv_pinned` or `long_context` get routed to FlashAttnV2-optimized devices; 4) Improve KV-cache continuous batching by allowing partial-batch KV stitching and stronger prefix caching heuristics; 5) Extensive unit and integration tests plus microbench harness. Testing & CI: local microbench harness shows steady improvements; CI initially failed on a flaky memory-alignment test which was fixed by aligning the kernel launch for odd-head counts. Rollout plan: canary on 5% of traffic for 24h, then 25% for 48h with automatic rollback if p95 latency regression > 10% or error rate > 0.1%. Notes: This is an internal implementation change with no public API changes. Callouts: quantized kernels will be a follow-up (ENG-4218).

fuse qkv + rotary application in attn_forward path
scheduler: add flashattn capability tag and routing hint

tests: add microbench harness and unit tests for fused ops
review_comments: Maya Chen: Great work — can you add a guard for older CUDA toolchains that don't support async copy? (resolved in commit 3)
Liam O'Connor: The scheduler hint name `kv_pinned` is a little vague, consider `attn_prefers_flashattn` for clarity. (author replied: renamed and added a mapping in routing_policy.cpp)
Priya Desai: microbench numbers look promising, can you include p99s as well as median? (added to bench output and docs)
CI bot: Memory alignment test failed on first run — reproduced locally and fixed by aligning shared memory loads for odd head counts (see commit 4)
Maya Chen: approve after CI green and canary plan added to PR description
ci_checks: perf-regression-check: pass (20-45% throughput uplift on tested models)
benchmarks: gpt-3.5-like, seq_len=4096, batch=1: throughput +32%, p99 latency -18%
llama-2-13b, seq_len=8192, batch=2: throughput +28%, p99 latency -22%
long-context streaming workload (mixed lengths): tokens/sec +45% for optimized device routing
notes: Follow-up work: quantized FlashAttn paths (ENG-4218), selector heuristics for small-batch edge cases, and improved telemetry for kernel-level failures.
migration_instructions: None. Runtime selects kernels automatically based on model shape and device capabilities. Operators can opt-out via environment flag REDWOOD_DISABLE_FLASHATTN_V2=true during the canary.
discussion_thread_summary: Thread covered CUDA compatibility, scheduler naming, benchmark completeness, and rollout safety. All reviewers signed off after small changes and CI green. Canary configured in deployment config to enable auto rollback on regressions.
